lab_tasks.instruction: Pick one real control you own (or the §5 prod-db access control) and write its product card: owner (exactly one human), customers in priority order, top-3 ranked backlog, the UX target, and the metrics — using the §5.1 shape.
lab_tasks.objective: O1 — describe a control as a product (customers, backlog, UX, owner, metrics)
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Parse the learner's product-card artifact (structured form or markdown): assert exactly one owner name (reject 'team'/'committee'/multiple names); assert >=2 customer types from {engineer, auditor, business} in an explicit priority order; assert >=3 backlog items present and ranked; assert UX-target field non-empty (bonus check: mentions 'evidence as a by-product'); assert >=4 metrics listed including a loss-exposure ($) metric.

lab_tasks.instruction: Open fixtures/risk-input.json. In words, state what the frequency range and magnitude range mean and why they're estimated separately.
lab_tasks.objective: O2 — understand the FAIR frequency/magnitude decomposition
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Verify the learner ran `cat`/`jq` on fixtures/risk-input.json in the sim terminal (file-read event in sim state); then grade a short structured answer: frequency = events/year (0.1-0.6), magnitude = USD/event (300000-2500000), separated because different evidence informs each (incident history vs value at stake). Multiple-choice or keyword match on 'events/year', 'dollars per event', 'different evidence'.

lab_tasks.instruction: Run the reference calculator (bun expected_loss.ts fixtures/risk-input.json) to compute the mean expected annual loss and the 95th-percentile bad year from the fixture. Record both numbers in your memo.
lab_tasks.objective: O2 — produce a mean and tail percentile from a sampling calculation
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Sim terminal command `bun expected_loss.ts fixtures/risk-input.json` returns deterministic JSON {mean: 493516, tailPercentile: 95, tailValue: 1133873, iterations: 10000} (LCG seed 42 is fully deterministic — port the LCG to JS in the sim for exact fidelity). Then assert the learner entered mean=493516 (accept ~$494k, 490000-497000 band) and tail=1133873 (accept ~$1.13M band) into the memo fields.

lab_tasks.instruction: Replace the fixture's ranges with your control's estimates and re-run. Confirm the mean and the tail move the way you'd expect (wider magnitude range → fatter tail). Write one sentence on why the tail, not the mean, is the executive's concern.
lab_tasks.objective: O2 — manipulate ranges and reason about distribution shape
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Sim tracks edits to risk-input.json (editor pane); assert at least one of frequency.min/max or magnitude.min/max changed from fixture defaults; re-run event recorded; sim recomputes with same LCG so new mean/tail are exact; assert learner's recorded new numbers match recompute; assert tail > mean in their result; grade the one-sentence tail rationale via keyword/rubric match ('bad year', 'worst case', 'tail risk', '1-in-20').

lab_tasks.instruction: Build the seven-stage scoring table for your control: for each of UNDERSTAND, LOCATE, QUERY, EVALUATE, EVIDENCE, MONITOR, OWN write the deciding question and your BUILD/BUY/HYBRID call with a one-line reason.
lab_tasks.objective: O3 — map all seven loop stages onto build/buy/hybrid
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Structured table builder: assert all 7 stages present (same assertion as happy-path.sh: each row has a call in {BUILD, BUY, HYBRID} and non-empty deciding question + reason). Soft-grade against the canonical pattern (UNDERSTAND=BUILD, OWN=BUILD always; LOCATE/QUERY/MONITOR lean BUY; EVALUATE leans BUILD; EVIDENCE leans HYBRID) — hard-fail only UNDERSTAND/OWN != BUILD since module states those are 'always own'; flag-and-explain for contrarian calls elsewhere if reason is empty.

lab_tasks.instruction: Draw the boundary line: one explicit paragraph stating which stages are vendor-owned, which are yours, and specifically why you own (or don't) the EVALUATE/policy-and-evidence layer. Name one case where the vendor abstraction wins and one where owning the library wins.
lab_tasks.objective: O4 — diagnose where vendor abstraction helps vs where owning beats it, avoiding NIH and vendor-worship
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Structured two-field input ('vendor wins because...' and 'owning wins because...'): assert BOTH fields non-empty and non-duplicate (single-direction argument = automatic fail per rubric); assert the boundary paragraph references EVALUATE explicitly; keyword/rubric grade for undifferentiated-breadth reasoning (vendor case) and posture-nuance reasoning (owning case: exceptions, compensating controls, crosswalks).

lab_tasks.instruction: Assemble tasks 1-6 into a single decision-memo.md ending with a one-paragraph recommendation that explicitly ties the boundary to the loss number from task 3 (e.g., 'we own EVALUATE because the $Xk/yr exposure lives in a posture the generic check can't model').
lab_tasks.objective: O5 — produce a finance-legible, risk-quantified build-vs-buy decision memo
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Assert decision-memo.md exists in sim filesystem and contains all five parts (product card, two loss figures, 7-row table, boundary paragraph, recommendation); assert the recommendation paragraph contains a dollar figure matching the task-3/4 computed mean or tail (regex for $ amount within tolerance of computed values); assert it reads as a decision (contains a build/buy/own verb directed at a stage), not a summary.

lab_setup_state: Offline, no cloud/vendor/network. labs/setup.sh writes fixtures/risk-input.json (FAIR-style input for the §5.2 scenario '12 standing prod-db access grants that never expire'): frequency 0.1-0.6 events/year, magnitude $300,000-$2,500,000/event, iterations 10000, tail_percentile 95, seed 42. labs/expected_loss.ts is a bun TypeScript reference calculator using a deterministic Numerical Recipes LCG (state = state*1664525 + 1013904223 mod 2^32, seeded 42) sampling uniform pairs, sorting losses, linear-interpolated percentile — exact output on fixture: mean 493516, tailValue 1133873. labs/happy-path.sh is the coreutils-only CI reproduction (awk srand-based sampling + 2000-bucket histogram p95, no sort) asserting fixture ranges unchanged, mean within ±5% of analytic 490000 (= 0.35 × 1,400,000), tail > mean (right-skew), and a 7-row scoring-table.tsv with valid BUILD/BUY/HYBRID calls. Learner needs bash + coreutils + awk; bun optional.
assessment_artifact: A build-vs-buy decision memo (decision-memo.md) for one control area, produced unaided in 120 minutes, with five mandatory parts mapped to rubric rows (all Pass/Not-yet, all must pass): (1) Product card — exactly one accountable owner, customers in deliberate priority order, ranked backlog of >=3 with highest-risk item near top, UX target (ideally 'evidence as a by-product'), >=4 observable metrics including loss exposure bought down; (2) Loss-exposure quantification — frequency and magnitude estimated separately as ranges with a one-line reason, run through a sampling calculation reporting mean AND tail percentile (point estimates or RAG cells fail outright), plus why the tail is the executive's concern; (3) Seven-stage BUILD/BUY/HYBRID scoring table with deciding question and one-line reason per stage; (4) Explicit owned-vs-vendor boundary paragraph with a specific EVALUATE-layer call and BOTH one honest vendor-wins case and one honest owning-wins case; (5) Risk-quantified recommendation tying the boundary explicitly to the Part-2 number in finance-legible terms (one-time cost vs recurring expected loss + tail). Reproducibility condition: reviewer re-running the stated ranges must land in the same band. Pass-rate threshold 0.80; 'Quantified gap' (O2) and 'Boundary judgment' (O4) are the early-warning rows.

exercise_design.sim_state: Virtual lab directory {labs/setup.sh, labs/expected_loss.ts, labs/fixtures/risk-input.json, (learner-created) decision-memo.md, scoring-table.tsv}; a risk-input document model (frequency/magnitude ranges, iterations, seed) shared between editor and calculator; a ported deterministic LCG sampler (exact JS reimplementation of expected_loss.ts — trivially portable since it IS JS/TS) so every run is bit-identical to the real tool; a memo document model accumulating the five parts; a scoring-table state object validated with the same assertions as happy-path.sh.
exercise_design.notes: This module is uniquely well-suited to a static web app because its reference calculator is already TypeScript with a seeded LCG — port computeExposure() verbatim and the sim achieves 100% output fidelity with zero backend. Recommended flow: (1) terminal-sim warmup — run setup.sh, cat the fixture, answer what each field means; (2) run bun expected_loss.ts in the terminal-sim and record mean=493516 / tail=1133873 into memo fields (exact-match verification); (3) interactive distribution explorer — sliders/editor bound to frequency/magnitude ranges with a live histogram showing mean vs p95; tasks like 'widen the magnitude max to $5M and observe the tail fatten' and 'why does uniform sampling understate the tail?' (the §4.5 lognormal caveat as a reflection question); (4) RAG-grid demolition mini-exercise — given a 5x5 colored grid and two priced options ($200k high vs 2×$50k mediums), show the grid cannot answer which to fund, then answer it with the sampler; (5) product-card structured builder with machine checks (one owner, prioritized customers, ranked backlog, metrics incl. $ exposure); (6) seven-stage scoring table builder reusing happy-path.sh's exact assertions (7 stages, valid calls, hard-fail UNDERSTAND/OWN != BUILD); (7) boundary builder forcing BOTH a vendor-wins and an owning-wins entry (the anti-NIH/anti-vendor-worship check is structural); (8) policy-exception scenario — vendor dashboard shows 'FAIL: unencrypted disk' for a risk-accepted public-data server; learner picks the defensible response (encode exception in owned policy layer vs manual quarterly override); (9) memo assembly — concatenate the artifacts into decision-memo.md and verify the recommendation cites the computed dollar figure. Free-text paragraphs (boundary, recommendation, tail rationale) need keyword/rubric heuristics or an optional LLM-grader; everything else is fully deterministic.

fidelity_notes: Two fidelity classes here. (1) expected_loss.ts is fully deterministic (LCG seed 42) and platform-independent — exact fixture output is mean=493516, tailValue=1133873; module §5.2 rounds these to ~$494,000 and ~$1,134,000. Port the LCG verbatim to the sim for perfect fidelity, and recompute exactly when the learner edits ranges. (2) happy-path.sh's awk path is NOT portable-deterministic: awk's srand(42)/rand() differs across implementations (macOS awk produced mean=$491867, p95=$1126125; gawk on Linux will produce different numbers). The script is designed for this — it asserts a ±5% band around the analytic mean (0.35 × 1,400,000 = $490,000) and tail>mean, never exact values. A sim reproducing happy-path.sh should either pin one implementation's verbatim PASS line (e.g., the macOS one above, or run once under gawk in docker for a Linux-canonical line) or render the PASS line from the sim's own sampler values, since any mean in [465500, 514500] with tail>mean is a legitimate run. Also note one inconsistency to avoid teaching as gospel: setup.sh defaults DEST to ./fixtures relative to CWD, so running it from the repo root vs labs/ writes to different paths — the sim should mirror the lab convention (run from labs/, fixture at labs/fixtures/risk-input.json). The committed fixture and the setup.sh-generated fixture are byte-identical. All free-text deliverables (boundary paragraph, recommendation) have no machine-exact ground truth — grade structurally (both-directions present, dollar figure cited, EVALUATE named) plus keyword heuristics.
